subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a native folder-backed encrypted snapshot and restore flow with new backup config keys, once the security findings and proof gap are fixed?
rationale: The PR adds a new core backup lifecycle, config surface, and destructive restore behavior; code review can identify blockers, but core product acceptance and upgrade/security policy need maintainer intent.

options.title: Continue as core backup PR
options.body: Require a rebase, the listed symlink/restore hardening fixes, upgrade/security review, and redacted real CLI proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to export hardening
options.body: Decline the new snapshot lifecycle for now and salvage only applicable hardening into the existing local archive backup path.

options.title: Route off-machine backup externally
options.body: Keep core focused on local export/verify and let off-machine or provider-specific backup live as a ClawHub/plugin integration such as the linked keepmyclaw-style approach.

recommendation.title: Continue as core backup PR
recommendation.body: Require a rebase, the listed symlink/restore hardening fixes, upgrade/security review, and redacted real CLI proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current local backup CLI feature and are the strongest maintainer-side routing signal in the observed history.
